Knowledge of policy-based and risk adaptive access controls.
Knowledge of root cause analysis techniques.
Knowledge of organizational information technology (IT) user security policies (e.g., account creation, password rules, access control).
Knowledge of current and emerging threats/threat vectors.
Knowledge of Risk Management Framework (RMF) process.
Knowledge of privacy principles and practices.
Knowledge of Security Classification Guide (SCG) purpose, interpretation, and format.
Knowledge of AT requirements, designs, technologies, and process for approval.
Develops security views and viewpoints as part of the system architecture and design – including any security boundaries and/or any physical, logical, or data elements of the system-of-systems.

Knowledge of cybersecurity principles and methods that apply to the software lifecycle, the software development process, software development environment and tooling, and software architecture and design methodologies.

Performs system security analyses, interprets the results of other system analyses, participates in system design reviews, and advocates for inherently secure system capabilities in support of decision-making as part of the overall product development team – including engineering, system operators, and other specialties.
Provides security considerations to inform systems engineering efforts with the objective to reduce errors, flaws, and weaknesses that may constitute a security vulnerability.

Reviews threat intelligence, emerging practices, lessons learned, and principles or tenets that can proactively inform improvements to the system to make it less susceptible to attacks throughout the system lifecycle
